solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Low rugby kick, dislodging head protection

indicators.note: dislodging the head means the first letter of the kick's name is knocked off

parts.note: in rugby union, the low kick that bobbles along the turf has its own name, a seven-letter word starting with G

explanation.surface: A rugby player's scuffed kick along the ground knocks off someone's headgear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head protection' reads as a helmet or scrum cap, but 'head' belongs to the deletion and 'protection' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A condom is colloquially called a rubber, and it is a form of protection in the contraceptive sense.

clue.text: Polish state council's inaugural rule of authority

parts.note: to polish something is to rub it
RI is the postal abbreviation for Rhode Island, a US state

indicators.note: the inaugural letter is the first one of the word council's

explanation.surface: A Polish state council lays down its first ruling as an authority.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' with its capital pretends to be the nationality; it is the verb meaning rub.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubric is a heading or instruction laying down how something is to be done, originally the red-lettered rules in liturgical books.

clue.text: Problem for driver — pond is awkwardly placed in Sandwich?

indicators.note: placed in tells us the shuffled letters go inside the sandwich

parts.note: a BLT is a bacon, lettuce and tomato sandwich

indicators.note: awkwardly suggests the letters of pond is are set out in a clumsy new order

explanation.surface: A driver finds a pond badly sited in Sandwich, the Kent town.
explanation.walkthrough: Sandwich, with its capital, poses as the town in Kent; it is the lunchtime kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A blind spot is the area a driver cannot see in the mirrors, a well-known hazard on the road.

clue.text: Level One swimming requires college assistance mostly

indicators.note: requires is read as the shuffled word taking in, or holding, the following pieces
swimming suggests the letters of one floating into a different order

parts.note: taken as written before shuffling

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: assistance means help

explanation.surface: A swimmer at level one needs a fair bit of help from the college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'requires' works as a container: the shuffled word needs, and so holds, the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: An echelon is a level or rank in an organisation, as in the upper echelons of management.

clue.text: Middle-aged fellow Tory excited single mum

indicators.note: excited suggests the letters of Tory are stirred up into a new order

parts.note: I, the Roman numeral one, stands for single
mum as in keeping mum means silent, and SH is the call for silence

explanation.surface: A middle-aged Conservative gets worked up about a lone mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'single mum' looks like one phrase but splits in two; 'mum' means quiet, not mother.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone of about forty years old is in the middle of life, hence middle-aged.

clue.text: Monster therefore must be overthrown

indicators.note: in a down clue, overthrown means the word is turned upside down, so read from bottom to top

parts.note: ergo is Latin for therefore

explanation.surface: A monster, so the story goes, has to be toppled.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogre is a man-eating giant of folklore, a classic monster.

clue.text: First given £1000, au pair regularly scrubbed palace

parts.note: top means first, as in top of the class
K, for kilo, is slang for a thousand pounds

indicators.note: regularly scrubbed means every other letter of au pair is wiped away, leaving the rest

explanation.surface: An au pair is paid a thousand pounds up front to scrub a palace clean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly scrubbed' removes U, A and R from AU PAIR, keeping A, P, I.
explanation.definitionFit: The Topkapi is the great Ottoman sultans' palace in Istanbul, now a museum.

clue.text: Like a Welshman making cream?

parts.note: Ivor is a typically Welsh man's name, as in Ivor Novello
the suffix -y means like or having the quality of, as in silky

explanation.surface: Asks what being Welsh has to do with making cream.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads 'like an Ivor': the name plus the adjective-forming -y.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivory is an off-white shade, very close to the colour called cream.

clue.text: Classical lady showing hesitation in greeting somebody

indicators.note: in means the hesitation sits inside the greeting

parts.note: hi is an informal greeting
erm is the sound of someone hesitating
one means somebody, as in one would think

explanation.surface: A refined lady hesitates when saying hello to someone.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Hermione is the daughter of Menelaus and Helen of Troy, a figure of classical legend.

clue.text: Damage front of bedside lamp

indicators.note: front of picks out the first letter of bedside

parts.note: a lamp is a light

explanation.surface: Something has damaged the front of a bedside lamp.
explanation.definitionFit: To blight something is to spoil or ruin it, so it works as a verb for damage.

clue.text: Crucifix role — revolutionary exit for thespian?

indicators.note: revolutionary means the two words together are turned round and read backwards

parts.note: a rood is a crucifix, especially one above a church screen
an actor's role is a part

explanation.surface: Playing the crucifix is a radical part, so how does the actor leave the stage?
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' turns ROODPART round as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage trapdoor lets an actor vanish through the floor, a classic theatrical exit.

clue.text: Informal discussion leaves children up-to-date

parts.note: tea is made from dried leaves
in means fashionable or current

explanation.surface: An informal chat leaves the children well informed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' looks like a verb but is the noun for tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A teach-in is an informal lecture and debate session, popular on campuses in the 1960s.

clue.text: Sort of undies placed around little guys initially. Pampers?

indicators.note: placed around means the shuffled letters wrap round the next ones
sort of suggests a rearranged version, a different sort, of the word undies
initially picks out the first letters of little and guys

explanation.surface: Pampers nappies are a kind of underwear wrapped round little boys.
explanation.walkthrough: Pampers is a nappy brand, but here it is the verb meaning spoils.
explanation.definitionFit: To pamper someone is to indulge them, treating them with excessive comfort.

clue.text: Annual fire, with one replacing backmost ancient manuscripts

parts.note: PA is short for per annum, meaning yearly

indicators.note: replacing backmost means the last letter of the fire word is swapped out for the one

parts.note: a pyre is a heap of wood for burning, a funeral fire
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An annual bonfire is lit, with one item replacing the hindmost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replacing backmost' turns PYRE into PYRI by putting I where the last letter E was.
explanation.definitionFit: Papyri are documents written on papyrus reed, the writing material of ancient Egypt.

clue.text: Hate avant-garde paintings deep down

indicators.note: avant-garde suggests the letters of hate are made experimental, rearranged into something new

parts.note: paintings are art

explanation.surface: Someone, deep down, hates modern experimental paintings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'avant-garde' rearranges HATE into ATHE.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying someone is kind at heart means fundamentally, underneath it all.

clue.text: Horrified, John denounced critic's knowledge

parts.note: the john is slang for a lavatory, and a pan is the toilet bowl

indicators.note: denounced suggests the letters of critic's are torn apart and set out anew

parts.note: the possessive 's is ignored; the word's letters are used
ken means knowledge, as in beyond my ken

explanation.surface: John is horrified that a critic's knowledge was publicly attacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'John' is a toilet, not a man. 'denounced' rearranges CRITICS into ICSTRIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Being stricken with sudden fear or alarm is close to being horrified.

clue.text: Fur pants, very loud in Leek, created commotion

indicators.note: in puts the scrambled fur and FF inside the other letters
created suggests the letters of Leek are made into something new
pants, as slang for rubbish, signals that the letters of fur are messed up

parts.note: FF, fortissimo, is the musical notation for very loud

explanation.surface: Fur trousers and very loud noise caused a stir in Leek.
explanation.walkthrough: Leek is a market town in Staffordshire; here it is just fodder, and 'pants' is British slang for rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: A kerfuffle is a fuss or disturbance, an everyday British word for a commotion.

clue.text: A rogue and accomplice finally end up getting life in an institution?

parts.note: a cad is a rogue or scoundrel

indicators.note: finally picks out the last letter of accomplice
in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: an end is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: A villain and his sidekick finally get life sentences in prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'institution' suggests a prison, and 'getting life' a sentence; the question mark flags that it is the university that is meant. 'up' turns AIM into MIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Academia is the world of universities, so it is life within an academic institution.

clue.text: Consort, running in the race, heard father

indicators.note: running suggests the letters of in the race scramble into a new order
heard means the word for father is said aloud, sounding like a surname

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: A runner in the race heard her father cheering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running' rearranges IN THE RACE into a woman's name, and 'heard' makes PA sound like PARR in non-rhotic British speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry VIII's sixth and last wife was his queen consort, the one who outlived him.

clue.text: Retirees from 17, heads of electronics industry, received special timer

indicators.note: received means the two initials take in the rearranged letters between them
heads of picks out the first letters of electronics and industry
special suggests the letters of timer are made into a particular new arrangement

explanation.surface: Retired staff, heads of the electronics industry, were given a special clock.
explanation.walkthrough: The 17 in the definition points to the answer at 17 down, the university world.
explanation.definitionFit: Emeriti are professors who have retired but keep their title as an honour.

clue.text: Mariner separated shellfish

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor
separated from others means alone

explanation.surface: A sailor became parted from his shellfish.
explanation.definitionFit: The abalone is an edible sea snail with an ear-shaped shell lined with mother-of-pearl.

clue.text: Complex housed finals in modern art — an unknown number passed

indicators.note: housed means the web word holds the following letters inside it

parts.note: a web is a complex network

indicators.note: finals in picks out the last letters of modern and art

parts.note: in algebra Y is an unknown quantity

explanation.surface: A building complex displayed the final pieces of modern art, and an unknown number of visitors passed through.
explanation.definitionFit: Time that went by has gone past, so the phrase is a phrasal verb for passed.

clue.text: Faulty line somewhere in the West Midlands

parts.note: a dud is something that does not work
a ley line is a supposed alignment of ancient sites, so ley means a line

explanation.surface: A faulty phone line somewhere in the Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Dudley is a large town in the West Midlands, the industrial region around Birmingham.

clue.text: Couple of naturists exchanging beach highlights?

indicators.note: exchanging means two letters of the word swap places, its first and third

parts.note: a pair of naturists are nudes

explanation.surface: A couple on a nudist beach swap places among the highlights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exchanging' swaps the N and D of NUDES.
explanation.definitionFit: Sand dunes are the high points of a beach, hence its highlights in a playful sense.

clue.text: Rook to consume when covered in salt. Food for carnivores?

indicators.note: when covered in means the rook and eating letters go inside the salting word

parts.note: to salt meat is to cure it
R is the chess abbreviation for rook
to consume food is to eat

explanation.surface: A rook eats salted food, served up for meat-eaters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'salt' is the verb, as in preserving meat, not the seasoning.
explanation.definitionFit: Any living animal is a creature, and carnivores eat animals, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Adversary stifled laughter, in principle — icy thing

indicators.note: stifled means the enemy word muffles that letter by holding it inside

parts.note: an adversary is a foe

indicators.note: in principle points to the principal, leading letter of laughter

explanation.surface: An enemy suppresses laughter, as a matter of principle, at something cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in principle' reads as 'theoretically'; here it means the principal (first) letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A floe is a sheet of floating ice, so literally an icy thing.

clue.text: Bony thing exercised limb outside with energy

indicators.note: outside means the shuffled limb letters go round the next word
exercised suggests the letters of limb are worked about into a new order

parts.note: with means and
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A bony limb is exercised outdoors to build energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exercised' rearranges LIMB into MIBL, which goes 'outside' AND as M-AND-IBL.
explanation.definitionFit: The mandible is the lower jaw bone.

clue.text: Bottom absent in model

indicators.note: in means the absent word goes inside the modelling word

parts.note: to sit for an artist is to model
someone off work is absent

explanation.surface: The model's backside is missing.
explanation.definitionFit: A soffit is the underside of an architectural feature, such as an arch or eaves.

clue.text: Rock hanger-on, getting excited, is able to meet Queen

indicators.note: excited suggests the letters of is able are stirred into a new order

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: A rock star's groupie gets excited at the chance to meet the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock hanger-on' suggests a groupie of a rock band, but it is a climber hanging off a cliff.
explanation.definitionFit: A climber descending a rope down a crag literally hangs on to the rock face.

clue.text: Irons pullover son left out, containing mark

indicators.note: containing means the shortened pullover holds the mark letter inside
left out means the son's letter is dropped

parts.note: a jersey is a pullover
M stands for mark, the former German currency

explanation.surface: Someone irons a pullover with a stain, leaving out their son's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Irons' looks like a verb about laundry; it is the actor's surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Jeremy Irons is the English actor, so his first name completes 'Irons'.
